Load the libraries

library(tidyverse)
library(janitor)
library(ggmap)
library(leaflet)

API Key

register_stadiamaps("efbbad0c-b639-4a5e-bc42-a820b574fc9b", write = FALSE)

Load the Data

For this homework, we will use the shark attack data to visualize where the attacks occurred. The data are from: State of California- Shark Incident Database.

sharks <- read_csv("data/SharkIncidents_1950_2022_220302.csv") %>% 
  clean_names() %>% 
  filter(longitude !="NA" & latitude !="NA") %>% # pulling out NA locations
  mutate(longitude = as.numeric(longitude)) # converting longitude to numeric
  1. Use the range of the latitude and longitude to build an appropriate bounding box for your map.
sharks %>% 
  summary()

lon_min <- -124.7
lon_max <- -117.1
lat_min <- 32.59
lat_max <- 41.56
lat <- c(lat_min, lat_max)
lon <- c(lon_min, lon_max)
  bbox <- make_bbox(lon, lat, f = 0.03)
  1. Load a map from stamen in a terrain style projection and display the map.
map_sharks <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom = 7)
## ℹ © Stadia Maps © Stamen Design © OpenMapTiles © OpenStreetMap contributors.
ggmap(map_sharks)

  1. Build a map that overlays the recorded observations of shark attacks in California.
ggmap(map_sharks) +
  geom_point(data = sharks, aes(longitude, latitude),  color = "red", alpha = 0.8, size = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Longitude",
       y = "Latitude",
       title = "California Shark Incidents (1950-2022)")

  1. Build a map that only shows the fatalities.
fatalities <- sharks %>% 
  filter(injury == "fatal")

ggmap(map_sharks) + 
  geom_point(data = fatalities, aes(longitude, latitude), size = 2, color = "red") +
  labs(title = "California Fatal Shark Incidents (1950-2022)")

  1. Build the same map (fatalities only), but this time make it interactive using leaflet. Also, color the points red.
leaflet(fatalities) %>% 
  addTiles() %>% 
  addProviderTiles(providers$Stadia.StamenTerrain) %>% 
  addCircleMarkers(
    lng = ~longitude,
    lat = ~latitude, 
    radius = 2,
    color = "red",
    stroke = FALSE,
    fillOpacity = 0.7
  ) %>% 
  addScaleBar(position = "bottomleft") %>% 
  fitBounds(lng1 = lon_min,
            lat1 = lat_min,
            lng2 = lon_max,
            lat2 = lat_max)
  1. Which county has the highest number of recorded shark attacks? Make a map that only shows the attacks in this county. (hint: it may help improve the map if you remove duplicate locations, i.e. multiple attacks at the same location.)
sharks %>% 
  count(county) %>% 
  arrange(desc(n))
## # A tibble: 21 × 2
##    county              n
##    <chr>           <int>
##  1 San Diego          24
##  2 San Mateo          19
##  3 Santa Barbara      19
##  4 Humboldt           18
##  5 Marin              16
##  6 Monterey           16
##  7 Santa Cruz         15
##  8 Sonoma             15
##  9 San Luis Obispo    14
## 10 Los Angeles         9
## # ℹ 11 more rows
top_county_data <- sharks %>% 
  filter(county == "San Diego") 
top_county_data %>% 
  summary()

lon_min <- -118.1

lat <- c(lat_min, lat_max)

  bbox <- make_bbox(lon, lat, f = 0.03)
map_sharks <- get_stadiamap(bbox, maptype = "stamen_terrain", zoom = 7)
